 Bizarre scenes as mystery drone halts A-League match: ‘It shouldn’t be flying around here’
 A drone paused Melbourne City's clash with Western Sydney Wanderers. Image source: Paramount+ 
 Sacha Pisani 
 November 7, 2026 
 share 
 Facebook 
 X 
 WhatsApp 
 LinkedIn 
 Melbourne City’s A-League Men showdown against Western Sydney Wanderers was temporarily halted in the first half due to a drone hovering over AAMI Park on Saturday night.
 The match came to a stop for almost three minutes as the referee and officials scrambled to identify the drone above the pitch, with City leading 1-0.
 Brazilian debutant Matheus Rossetto had given City a fourth-minute lead thanks to his stunning strike before the clash was briefly paused entering the 16th minute.
 Into the A-League? Get discounts on tickets and win unique matchday experiences with Football360. See the benefits here > 
 “We’re hearing there’s a drone above the stadium,” said Network 10 commentator Ben Homer.
 “It’s not our drone, it’s not a broadcast drone. They’re trying to work out whose drone that is and whether they can get rid of it.
 “… it certainly shouldn’t be flying around here at AAMI Park.”
 As the match resumed, Homer continued: “So apparently the drone has flown away and we’re all good to continue.”
 The bizarre scenes at AAMI Park come less than two weeks after Arsenal’s EFL Cup clash with Fleetwood Town was temporarily suspended because of an unauthorised drone hovering above the pitch.
 Last month’s encounter at Highbury Stadium was halted less than two minutes after kick-off when referee Michael Salisbury spotted the drone. Play was stopped for approximately eight minutes as officials consulted both managers and stadium security, while police worked to identify the operator.
 Players were preparing to leave the field before the drone disappeared and authorities reportedly located the person responsible, allowing the match to resume. The incident overshadowed the opening stages of a remarkable cup upset, with fourth-tier Fleetwood eventually eliminating Premier League champions Arsenal on penalties.
